# Ontology concordance {#sec:ontology-concordance}

<!-- generated by scripts/render_docs.py from data/ontology_concordance.json -->

The supplement compares what shared terms name in the finite models.
Source usage and distinctions describe terminology. Model correspondences,
conditional identities, counterexamples and geometric comparisons point to
the registry for their executable evidence. The scope column identifies
assumptions and the limits of the comparison.

The structured records in `data/ontology_concordance.json` give stable
term identifiers, meanings by programme and pointers to cited identifiers
in the pinned source register. Run `oph-fep-synergetics verify --key KEY`
to inspect the values for a listed probe.

## Interfaces and representations

| Term | Meaning by programme | Relationship and scope | Evidence |
|:-------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------|
| Patch | **OPH.** A local subsystem specified by its own state variables, stored records and allowed operations at its interface. | **Source usage.** The finite carrier describes one local model. Patch extent and physical scale remain open. | [@oph; @mueller2026observers] |
| Boundary | **OPH.** An access interface specified by the patch model. **FEP.** The variables separating interior and exterior in a probability model. **Synergetics.** A geometric surface, such as the faces of a Voronoi cell. | **Distinction.** Access rules, conditional independence and geometric incidence define different boundary structures. | [@oph; @pearl1988probabilistic; @quadmath] |
| Port | **OPH.** A boundary coordinate with an integer load on the finite carrier. **FEP.** A variable indexed by the corresponding carrier vertex. | **Model correspondence.** The Gaussian state space uses the carrier's indexing. A choice of model specifies which ports are recorded. | `carrier-port-chart`, `gmrf-independence`. [@oph; @mueller2026agreement] |
| Seam | **OPH.** A carrier edge across which a repair can transfer load. **FEP.** An off-diagonal coupling of the proper Gaussian precision on the carrier. | **Model correspondence.** The same adjacency describes allowed local repairs and the conditional-dependence graph of the specified Gaussian. | `native-repair-law`, `gmrf-independence`. [@oph; @mueller2026agreement] |
| Markov blanket | **FEP.** A set of variables that renders the interior and exterior conditionally independent. | **Counterexample.** The proper carrier Gaussian gives neighbour blankets. A stationary blanket can coexist with direct coupling in the drift. | `gmrf-independence`, `stationary-blanket`. [@pearl1988probabilistic; @mueller2026agreement] |
| Screen | **OPH.** The source constructs spherical screens by joining carriers. **FEP.** The cited quantum formulation reads a Markov blanket as an information boundary. | **Source usage.** The executable comparison concerns one finite carrier. The screen constructions supply context. | [@mueller2026observers; @fields2022generic] |

## Dynamics and inference

| Term | Meaning by programme | Relationship and scope | Evidence |
|:-------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------|
| Agreement | **OPH.** Adjacent carrier values satisfy their seam restrictions. **FEP.** The same quadratic form penalises disagreement in the scalar Gaussian sheaf model. | **Model correspondence.** For the chosen restrictions, agreement is a global section. The condition specifies compatible assignments separately from their reachability. | `sheaf-agreement`, `sheaf-cohomology`. [@mueller2026agreement] |
| Native repair | **OPH.** A seam acts on the loads at its endpoints with an integer transfer. **FEP.** On the binary shell its law is conditional resampling of the reference at the preserved datum. | **Conditional identity.** The conditioning reading uses a fair coin and uniform binary reference. A doubled load supplies a counterexample for the uniform full shell. | `native-repair-law`, `repair-is-conditioning`, `binary-conditional-variance`. [@oph; @mueller2026agreement] |
| Descent and termination | **OPH.** The ungated rule can change state at constant load energy. The broken-seam rule permits only strict decreases. **FEP.** Ensemble divergence to the binary reference is nonincreasing under uniform attempts. | **Counterexample.** On the total-load-two shell, the ungated relation is confluent and can cycle. The gated relation terminates with multiple reachable normal forms. | `pr01-obstruction`. [@oph; @mueller2026agreement] |
| Record | **OPH.** A declared observed quantity. For a fixed seam on the binary shell, the preserved datum is its total load and the loads elsewhere. **FEP.** A conditioned variable in the inference model. | **Conditional identity.** The datum depends on the protocol. The selector control uses a signed current as a different record that can affect the next repair. | `repair-is-conditioning`, `reduction-criterion`. [@oph; @mueller2026agreement] |
| Posterior inference | **OPH.** Harmonic extension minimises interface disagreement at fixed records on the scalar carrier. **FEP.** The Gaussian posterior mean has the same value in the stated model. | **Conditional identity.** The carrier comparison fixes the likelihood model and record prior. The asymmetric nonquadratic control separates the energy minimum from the posterior mean. | `variational-equivalence`, `two-record-resistance`. [@friston2010; @mueller2026agreement] |
| Energy and surprisal | **OPH.** Load energy is quadratic in the loads. Interface energy measures seam disagreement. **FEP.** Variational free energy separates into normalised record surprisal and divergence from the posterior. | **Distinction.** Fixed-record interface minima, unnormalised record potentials and normalised surprisals carry different normalisation terms. | `free-energy-name-collision`, `free-energy-dictionary`. [@oph; @friston2010; @mueller2026agreement] |
| Mean and ensemble | **OPH.** The mean update acts on port-load vectors. The binary attempt kernel acts on probabilities over configurations. **FEP.** The comparison on the proper carrier Gaussian reuses the Laplacian as a precision term. | **Model correspondence.** The two relaxation gaps agree under uniform seam attempts and a fair coin. The state spaces and their observables differ. | `spectral-gap`, `certificate-species`, `pr01-obstruction`. [@oph; @mueller2026agreement] |

## Shells and geometry

| Term | Meaning by programme | Relationship and scope | Evidence |
|:-------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------|
| Load shell | **OPH.** The load configurations with a fixed total on the carrier. **FEP.** The binary subset is the support of the reference used for the conditioning comparison. | **Model correspondence.** Shell membership concerns a full load configuration. The binary subset adds an occupancy restriction at each port. | `shell-counts`, `repair-is-conditioning`. [@oph; @mueller2026agreement] |
| Port-distance shell | **OPH.** Ports at fixed graph distance from a chosen port. **Synergetics.** IVM coordination counts use the lattice neighbour moves. | **Counterexample.** The carrier's port-distance counts differ from coordination counts on the IVM lattice. | `vertex-shells`. [@oph; @quadmath] |
| Coordination shell | **FEP.** Equal-covariance Gaussian divergence from the origin measures a squared displacement. **Synergetics.** Lattice sites at fixed shortest-path distance from the lattice origin. | **Counterexample.** The cuboctahedral gauge gives the coordination index. A shell contains multiple divergence levels, and a divergence level can intersect several shells. | `quadray-ivm`, `shell-vs-free-energy`. [@quadmath; @conway1997lowdim] |
| Quadray coordinates | **Synergetics.** Coordinates with a common-offset redundancy. Specified neighbour moves generate the IVM sublattice. | **Geometric comparison.** The integer embedding identifies FCC sites and tetrahedral and octahedral holes by quadray residue. Gaussian displacement costs use its specified scale. | `quadray-ivm`, `kl-lattice-metric`. [@quadmath; @fuller1975synergetics] |
| Kissing arrangement | **OPH.** The finite carrier has icosahedral incidence. **Synergetics.** The vector equilibrium is the cuboctahedral arrangement of nearest IVM neighbours. | **Geometric comparison.** Equal kissing counts allow different outer contacts and graph degrees. Geometric incidence distinguishes the solids. | `kissing-twelve`, `cuboctahedron-vs-icosahedron`, `carrier-spectral-chords`. [@oph; @quadmath; @schutte1953dreizehn] |
| Tetravolume | **OPH.** The carrier solid has an algebraic volume in the chosen unit. **Synergetics.** Volume measured in units of the tetrahedron whose edge is the prime vector. | **Geometric comparison.** A shared unit permits comparison between volumes of different solids. The rhombic-dodecahedral Voronoi cell belongs to the IVM lattice. | `icosahedron-tetravolume`, `packing-density`, `tetravolume-arithmetic`. [@quadmath; @fuller1975synergetics] |

## Exact reductions and geometric limits

| Term | Meaning by programme | Relationship and scope | Evidence |
|:-------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------|
| First binary entry | **OPH.** The first fair attempt that splits a doubled load into occupations at adjacent ports. **FEP.** A stopping-time law and an entrance distribution on the closed binary state space. | **Counterexample.** A uniform doubled start gives the same single-port marginals at entry as at stationarity. Their joint laws differ. | `repair-first-entry`. [@oph; @kemeny1976finite] |
| Distance quotient | **OPH.** The separation of the loaded units projected to graph distance, with distance zero for a doubled load. **FEP.** A Markov reduction and a class-uniform lift, with a relative entropy identity on the binary block. **Synergetics.** The carrier intersection array counts inward and outward moves. | **Conditional identity.** The quotient uses uniform seam choice and fair repair on the load-two shell. Exact reconstruction of the full law also uses class uniformity. | `repair-distance-lumping`, `vertex-shells`. [@oph; @kemeny1976finite] |
| Grounded precision | **OPH.** Fix selected carrier ports as records and retain the interior seam Laplacian. **FEP.** The determinant of the conditional precision controls conditional differential entropy at a fixed record budget. | **Conditional identity.** Each counted spanning forest has one record in each component. Greedy placement can miss the least uncertain triple. | `grounded-forest-precision`, `greedy-record-placement`. [@oph; @chaiken1982minors] |
| Dual edge covariance | **OPH.** Each oriented carrier seam has a corresponding edge between its incident faces. **FEP.** Primal and dual Gaussian edge differences have complementary covariance projectors. **Synergetics.** The cuboctahedral neighbour shell and rhombic dodecahedral cell form a second dual pair. | **Conditional identity.** The projector sum uses unit edge precision and consistent edge orientations on the spherical complexes. | `planar-dual-covariance`, `dual-cells`. [@oph; @quadmath; @furrer2020resistors] |
| Spectral chord | **OPH.** The carrier's slowest nonconstant mean-repair eigenspace recovers its Euclidean coordinates up to scale. **FEP.** Contrast variance from the lowest nonconstant modes is proportional to squared chord length in the tested models. **Synergetics.** The cuboctahedral shell has two chord lengths at graph distance two. | **Geometric comparison.** The proportionality uses a projected covariance and a specified edge scale. On the FCC shell, full variance splits the middle graph-distance class. | `carrier-spectral-chords`, `cuboctahedral-spectral-chords`, `cuboctahedral-distance-split`. [@quadmath; @klein1993resistance; @osting2023extremal] |

## Three-way correspondences and counterexamples

| Term | Meaning by programme | Relationship and scope | Evidence |
|:-------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------|
| Contrast record | **OPH.** A scalar readout of the occupied pair in fair binary seam repair. **FEP.** The intrinsic variance of the difference between the two port fields groups states into an exact Markov quotient. **Synergetics.** Squared chords distinguish the FCC pair orbits, including two orbits at distance two. | **Conditional identity.** The same uniform-seam, fair-coin protocol applies to both graphs. FCC graph distance alone retains memory even under stationarity. | `repair-contrast-quotient`, `repair-distance-counterexample`. [@oph; @quadmath; @kemeny1976finite] |
| Centroid memory | **OPH.** The local seam law evolves the occupied pair whose geometric centroid is observed. **FEP.** A sampled isotropic Gaussian diffusion matches all lag covariances. Three-time probabilities distinguish the repair process. **Synergetics.** Opposite loaded pairs collapse to the same centroid on both shells. | **Counterexample.** The result compares stationary second moments and exact three-time probabilities for the binary protocol on static graphs. | `repair-centroid-memory`. [@oph; @quadmath; @uhlenbeck1930brownian] |
| Reciprocal edge precision | **OPH.** Oriented carrier seams supply a matched edge basis for the carrier and its face dual. **FEP.** Energy-normalised edge covariances give complementary projectors exactly at constant primal–dual conductance product. **Synergetics.** The cuboctahedral first shell and the Voronoi cell furnish the second spherical dual pair. | **Conditional identity.** Weights must be positive and edge signs matched. Copying even one nonuniform weight breaks complementarity. | `reciprocal-dual-weights`, `copied-dual-weight-obstruction`. [@oph; @quadmath; @furrer2020resistors] |
| Quadratic field | **OPH.** The sampled trace-free quadratic spans the centred antipodally even port fields. **FEP.** Pulling back the seam precision yields a Gaussian on the coefficients of the quadratic. **Synergetics.** The cuboctahedral directions split the diagonal and off-diagonal quadratic variances. | **Geometric comparison.** Use unit vertex directions and unit seam precision. Equal linear frame isotropy leaves different fourth moments. | `quadratic-even-field`, `quadratic-isotropy-obstruction`. [@oph; @quadmath; @delsarte1977codes] |
| Central-plane screen | **OPH.** Ports on a geometric plane are treated as fixed records on the carrier. **FEP.** The strict half-fields are conditionally independent when the reduced precision has zero cross-block entries. **Synergetics.** The FCC coordinate and body-diagonal equators cut all crossing seams. Carrier equators leave crossing seams. | **Counterexample.** The Gaussian is scalar with seam support. The conditional information values use the grounded unit Laplacian. | `central-plane-screening`. [@oph; @quadmath; @dempster1972covariance] |

: Three-way correspondences and counterexamples in the compared models. {#tbl:ontology-three-way-transfer}

\clearpage

## Transfer criteria beyond the two shells

| Term | Meaning by programme | Relationship and scope | Evidence |
|:-------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------|
| Distance regularity | **OPH.** Uniform fair seam repair gives inward and outward move counts. **FEP.** Gaussian contrast variance labels the same exact quotient. **Synergetics.** A distance-regular graph has fixed intersection counts within each distance. | **Conditional identity.** For connected simple regular graphs, distance regularity is also necessary for the distance quotient. | `distance-regular-repair`. [@oph; @biggs1993potential] |
| Resistance collision | **OPH.** Equal observations can hide different one-step seam moves. **FEP.** Equal effective resistance need not give a Markov record. **Synergetics.** Periodic FCC displacements can agree in variance, distance and common-neighbour count. | **Counterexample.** Compare other-class probabilities. In the periodic example the failure persists at stationarity. | `bipartite-contrast-collision`, `periodic-fcc-contrast-collision`. [@oph; @quadmath; @kemeny1976finite] |
| Covariance closure | **OPH.** A fair seam attempt is a mixture of identity and an endpoint swap. **FEP.** An invariant linear observation space has the lag covariances of a Gaussian Markov process. **Synergetics.** Unit seams preserve the coordinate space of the twenty-four-cell. One strengthened seam breaks invariance. | **Conditional identity.** The match concerns stationary second moments. The observed process can retain memory. | `linear-lag-closure`, `single-seam-lag-obstruction`. [@oph; @cohn2007d4; @caputo2010aldous] |
| Harmonic remainder | **OPH.** Vertex and oriented face incidences define two weighted seam spaces. **FEP.** Reciprocal Gaussian covariances leave a harmonic projector of rank twice the genus. **Synergetics.** The periodic square cellulation has two independent winding directions. | **Conditional identity.** A fixed trace does not certify positivity. Copying a nonuniform weight can make the remainder indefinite. | `surface-harmonic-covariance`, `copied-surface-weight-obstruction`. [@oph; @degoes2016exterior] |
| Root-shell quadratics | **OPH.** The scalar seam operator acts on trace-free even vertex fields. **FEP.** Diagonal and off-diagonal coefficient precisions are equal only in dimension four in this family. **Synergetics.** The cuboctahedral shell extends to the nearest-neighbour graphs of the signed two-coordinate roots. | **Geometric comparison.** Use unit vertex directions, unit seams, and the Frobenius metric. | `root-shell-quadratic-precision`. [@oph; @quadmath; @cohn2007d4] |
| Global sum constraint | **OPH.** Grounding a plane clamps the separator ports. **FEP.** A separate total-field constraint introduces rank-one dependence between the strict sides. **Synergetics.** The coordinate and body-diagonal FCC cuts have no crossing seams at any frequency. | **Counterexample.** Exact conditioning gives infinite conditional mutual information. Noisy sums give finite dependence. | `fcc-plane-screen-transfer`, `centered-gaussian-screen-obstruction`. [@oph; @quadmath; @bolin2021sparse] |

: Transfer criteria beyond the two shells in the compared models. {#tbl:ontology-transfer-beyond-shells}

## Jitterbug geometry and seam models

| Term | Meaning by programme | Relationship and scope | Evidence |
|:-------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------------|:------------------------|
| Jitterbug branch | **OPH.** The regular icosahedral hull realises the carrier. **Synergetics.** Rigid triangles preserve bar length from the vector equilibrium to the octahedron. | **Geometric comparison.** The branch describes joint locations at fixed bar length. The central-sphere contact protocol uses a different rescaling. | `jitterbug-rigid-motion`. [@oph; @fuller1975synergetics; @verheyen1989jitterbug; @stachel1994heureka; @kusner2018spheres] |
| Hull diagonal | **OPH.** The carrier seams include the bars and six short diagonals. **Synergetics.** The diagonals split the skew regions and form a perfect matching. | **Counterexample.** Hull, bar and nearest-pair graphs encode different data. The matching becomes equal in length to the bars only at the golden-ratio landmark. | `jitterbug-graph-obstruction`. [@oph; @fuller1975synergetics; @fuller1979synergetics2] |
| Matching conductance | **OPH.** Fair repair samples seams in proportion to weight. **FEP.** Weights set Gaussian contrasts and the precision determinant. **Synergetics.** The coordinate ratio fixes the weight that preserves the coordinate modes. | **Conditional identity.** The unique tuning applies to each fixed pose with distinct joints on the contraction branch. It matches stationary second moments of the coordinates. | `jitterbug-weighted-precision`, `jitterbug-coordinate-closure`. [@oph; @fuller1979synergetics2; @stachel1994heureka] |
| Nearest-only seams | **OPH.** Nearest-only repair conserves each dimer load. **FEP.** Global centering leaves five precision null modes. **Synergetics.** Past regularity, nearest joints form six disjoint pairs. | **Counterexample.** Contracting the nearest graph removes its internal dimer edges. Rebuilding nearest neighbours on the distinct endpoint sites gives the octahedral graph. | `jitterbug-nearest-only-obstruction`. [@oph; @fuller1975synergetics] |
| Conductance rule | **OPH.** Weights set fair repair sampling probabilities. **FEP.** A lag-two defect rules out Gaussian Markov closure. **Synergetics.** Short diagonal lengths define inverse-square weights. | **Counterexample.** Past regularity, the unit hull fails. Inverse-square weights close only at the half-ratio pose. | `jitterbug-weight-policy-obstruction`. [@oph; @stachel1994heureka] |
| Hard equality of pair values | **OPH.** Two bars supply parallel conductance. **FEP.** Infinite matching weight gives site precision twice the unit octahedral Laplacian. **Synergetics.** Each octahedral site contains a joint pair. | **Conditional identity.** The model uses unit bars and a centred scalar field. The reduced coordinates are the common pair values. | `jitterbug-octahedral-gaussian-limit`. [@fuller1975synergetics; @bolin2021sparse] |
| Observed pair load | **OPH.** Which label carries a token affects the next repair. **FEP.** A stationary three-time witness detects count memory. **Synergetics.** Coalesced joints keep distinct bar labels. | **Counterexample.** The witness uses finite matching weight and fair binary repair at the half-ratio pose. | `jitterbug-pair-load-memory`. [@oph; @fuller1975synergetics] |
| Averaged pair repair | **OPH.** Fast within-pair mixing gives capacity-two transfer. **FEP.** Linear lag covariances match Gaussian Markov decay. **Synergetics.** Two bars occupy each quotient edge. | **Conditional identity.** Scale the clock by total attempt weight before sending the matching weight to infinity. | `jitterbug-averaged-repair-limit`. [@oph; @stachel1994heureka; @giardina2009duality] |
| Moving coordinate readout | **OPH.** Each departure-pose update preserves the uniform two-token law. **FEP.** The middle-coordinate Gaussian Markov identity has a signed residual. **Synergetics.** Fixed bars link the same labels while their positions change. | **Counterexample.** Two attempts at prescribed distinct-joint departure poses with unit bars and individually tuned closing weights. Holding either leg fixed gives a zero residual. | `jitterbug-moving-closure-obstruction`. [@oph; @stachel1994heureka] |
| Fixed sign-supported slots | **OPH.** Both mean repair operators preserve the six linear slots. **FEP.** A Gaussian state-space model matches their lag covariances. **Synergetics.** Two slot coefficients per axis recover the coordinates in every pose. | **Conditional identity.** Stationary marginal and lag covariances for prescribed finite schedules of nonnegative matching weights. The dimension bound applies to fixed linear spaces containing the coordinates at two poses. | `jitterbug-augmented-lag-realization`. [@oph; @stachel1994heureka; @kalman1960filtering] |
| Finite projection onto closing pairs | **OPH.** Observed pair totals retain a lag-two covariance defect. **FEP.** Marginal pair-mean precision has a positive opposite-site entry. **Synergetics.** Pairing joint labels defines site means and hidden internal differences. | **Counterexample.** Unit bars, finite common matching conductance, a centred Gaussian field and fair repair on the binary two-token shell. The Gaussian sign test concerns literal arithmetic means. | `jitterbug-pair-projection-defect`. [@oph; @fuller1975synergetics; @dorfler2013kron] |
